versions.rustc: 1.88.0 (6b00bc388 2025-06-23), LLVM 20.1.5, same binary for native and wasm
versions.nativeFlags: rustc -O (matrix image languages/rust/Dockerfile, no other flags)

asymmetries: no target-cpu on either side; the wasm default feature set (bulk-memory, multivalue, mutable-globals, nontrapping-fptoint, reference-types, sign-ext) is rustc's baseline for the target, no simd128
native std links glibc (system malloc), wasm std ships its own dlmalloc
wasm shadow stack raised to 8 MiB to match the native 8 MiB main-thread stack
the native column is aarch64 machine code, so ratios mix ISA with wasm cost

panic strategy: rustc 1.88.0 builds wasm32-wasip1 with panic=abort (target default) and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu with panic=unwind (verified with rustc --print cfg); the wasm code has no unwinding landing pads. Kept: forcing one strategy on both would move the native build away from the matrix binary
wasm32 is ILP32: usize and pointers are 32-bit (all 18 sources are correct unchanged)
